chunks: From him, by his chain, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Hallal who said:
I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'A man from our companions gives me a book but does not say to me, "Narrate it from me." Is it permissible for me to narrate it from him?'
He (the narrator) said: So he (the Imam) said: 'When you know that the book belongs to him, then narrate it from him.'

key_terms.إجازة: Permission/authorization — the formal granting of authority to transmit a text
key_terms.ارو: Narrate/transmit — the technical term for transmitting a hadith with attribution to its source
key_terms.الكتاب: The book — a written collection of hadiths or scholarly notes (referring to early manuscript collections)
key_terms.يجوز: Is it permissible — a jurisprudential inquiry about the lawfulness of an action

ai.seo_question: Can you narrate from a hadith book without explicit permission from its author in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Ahmad ibn Umar al-Hallal asked Imam al-Ridha (AS) about the permissibility of narrating from a book given by a companion who did not explicitly grant permission to narrate from him. The Imam ruled that if one knows with certainty that the book belongs to that companion, narrating from him is permissible — implicit authorization (ijazah) is sufficient. This ruling reflects the hadith transmission norms of the early Islamic period, where formal verbal authorization was standard, but the Imam clarified that confirmed ownership of a book constitutes implicit permission.
